t: Under the amended Section 194E, not giving way to an ambulance or other emergency vehicle attracts:
o: Community service only
Fine of ₹10,000 and/or imprisonment up to six months
Fine of ₹500
Fine of ₹1,000
e: Section 194E (new): fine ₹10,000 or imprisonment up to six months or both; it supports the golden-hour objective of the amendment.

t: Under Section 81, a permit (other than a temporary permit) is effective from the date of issue or renewal for:
o: Ten years
One year
Three years
Five years
e: Section 81 fixes a five-year validity for permits; s.87 temporary permits are limited to four months.

t: An award of ₹12,00,000 carries 7.5% simple interest for 365 days, shared equally by four claimants. The TDS position on interest is:
o: TDS of ₹18,000 in total at 20%
TDS of ₹9,000 in total at 10%
TDS of ₹2,250 from each claimant
No TDS, as each claimant's interest of ₹22,500 does not exceed ₹50,000
e: Interest = 90,000; per claimant 22,500, below the ₹50,000 threshold, so no TDS is deducted.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
o: Sections 39 and 38
Sections 38 and 39
Sections 41 and 45
Sections 45 and 41
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Under Section 169, for the purpose of adjudicating claims the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal:
o: Has all the powers of a Civil Court and is deemed to be a Civil Court
Has the powers of a Magistrate of the first class
Is bound by the strict rules of the Code of Civil Procedure
Has the powers of a Labour Court under the Industrial Disputes Act
e: Section 169 confers on the Claims Tribunal all the powers of a Civil Court and deems it a Civil Court for all purposes, while allowing a summary procedure.

t: With effect from the IRDAI circular of 18 October 2023, legal liability to employees of the insured travelling in or driving a private car (IMT-29) is:
o: Available only under the Own Damage section
An inbuilt compulsory cover under the third party liability section of a private car policy without additional premium
An optional endorsement at ₹50 additional premium per employee
Excluded from all private car policies
e: IMT-29 was earlier an optional add-on at ₹50 extra premium; from October 2023 it is inbuilt in the TP liability section of private car package, bundled and stand-alone liability policies.

topic: Third party – who is a third party
t: A stage carriage bus with a registered capacity of 52 carries 50 passengers; the bus falls into a gorge due to the driver's negligence, killing 20. Under the Act policy, the passengers are:
o: Covered only under the compulsory PA cover
Covered only up to ₹5 lakh each under Section 164 with no further claim
Not third parties, since they contracted with the bus owner
Third parties whose death is covered under Section 147 as passengers of a transport vehicle
e: Section 147(1)(b)(ii) covers death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a transport vehicle (except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle) up to registered capacity.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
o: Section 140
Section 146
Section 163A
Section 166
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
Bharat Griha Raksha
Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha
Householder's Package Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: An injured claimant with a pending Section 166 petition dies of a heart attack unconnected with the accident injuries. Under the amended Act:
o: The claim abates completely under Section 306 of the Indian Succession Act
The right to claim compensation for the injury survives to his legal representatives irrespective of whether the death had any nexus with the injury
Only the medical expenses already incurred can be claimed by the heirs
The claim survives only if death was caused by the accident injuries
e: The 2019 amendment to s.166 provides that the right to claim compensation for injury survives to the legal representatives whether or not the cause of death is related to the injury.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
o: ₹50 crore
₹200 crore
₹100 crore
₹500 crore
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: The Tribunal awards ₹44,000 as compensation plus interest; the insurer disputes the entire amount. The maximum deposit payable with the appeal, if an appeal were maintainable, would be ₹22,000. In fact:
o: Appeal lies to the District Court instead
Appeal lies on deposit of ₹22,000
No appeal lies at all, since the amount in dispute is below ₹1,00,000
Appeal lies on deposit of ₹25,000
e: Irrespective of the deposit arithmetic (lower of ₹25,000 or 50%), s.173(2) bars appeals where the amount in dispute is less than one lakh rupees.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: A passer-by takes an injured accident victim to hospital. The hospital insists on his personal details and the police want to summon him repeatedly. Under Section 134A:
o: He is deemed a witness to negligence and must be impleaded
He is protected from civil or criminal liability and may give evidence by affidavit or video conferencing at his convenience
He becomes liable for the victim's treatment cost
He must appear personally before the Tribunal in every hearing
e: Section 134A protects Good Samaritans who voluntarily and without expectation of reward help a victim; rules provide for examination at their convenience and evidence through affidavit/video conferencing.

t: In the Challa Bharathamma case, the Supreme Court interpreted 'owner of the goods' under Section 147 to mean:
o: The consignee named in the lorry receipt, even if not travelling
The person who owned the goods and was travelling with them in the cabin of the goods vehicle
Any passenger carried in the goods vehicle
The driver of the goods vehicle
e: Only the owner of the goods (or his authorised representative) actually travelling with the goods is covered; other persons in a goods vehicle are gratuitous passengers and excluded.

t: Under the motor accident claims scheme (Rule 150A / CMV Rules, effective 01.04.2022), the Investigating Officer must submit the First Accident Report (Form I) to the Claims Tribunal within:
o: 90 days of the accident
30 days of the accident
10 days of the accident
48 hours of the accident
e: The FAR (Form I) goes to the Tribunal within 48 hours; Form II (rights of victims) within 10 days; the Interim Accident Report (Form V) within 50 days and the Detailed Accident Report (Form VII) within 90 days.

t: Under Section 164, the fixed compensation payable in the case of death is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 164 provides ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt, payable by the owner or insurer without proof of wrongful act or neglect.

t: A truck insured under an Act policy is driven by a person whose licence had been suspended for six months and the accident occurs during the suspension. The insurer's position under Section 150(2):
o: Breach of the specified condition regarding a disqualified driver is available as a defence
The insurer must pay and cannot recover from the owner under any circumstances
The defence is available only if the owner was also driving
No defence is available since the driver once held a valid licence
e: Section 150(2)(a)(ii) allows the insurer to defend on the ground of driving by a person not duly licensed or disqualified from holding a licence during the period of disqualification.

t: Under Section 166, an application for compensation may be made by:
o: The injured person, the owner of damaged property, the legal representatives of the deceased, or a duly authorised agent
The injured person only
The investigating police officer on behalf of the victim
The insurer of the offending vehicle
e: Section 166(1) lists the injured person, the owner of the property, all or any legal representatives where death has resulted, and any agent duly authorised by them.

t: A claimant files a Section 166 petition without pleading negligence of the driver and leads no evidence on it. The insurer objects. The Tribunal:
o: Must dismiss or reject the claim under Section 166, since fault liability requires negligence to be pleaded and proved; the claimant could instead have invoked Section 164
Must refer the case to the police for investigation
Must award ₹5 lakh under Section 166
Must award compensation, since negligence is presumed in all motor accidents
e: Section 166 is a fault-based remedy; negligence must be pleaded and proved. Section 164 is the no-fault route with fixed amounts.

t: A driving licence expired in January 2023 and the holder applies for renewal in June 2024. Under Section 15 he must:
o: Undergo a fresh driving test, as more than one year has elapsed since expiry
Pay a late fee only
Produce a medical certificate only
Obtain a fresh learner's licence and wait 30 days only
e: Where renewal is sought more than one year after expiry, a fresh test of competence is required; within the one-year grace period only the fee/late fee applies.

t: Under the pre-amendment Section 161, hit-and-run compensation for death and grievous hurt was respectively:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The old Solatium Scheme amounts were ₹25,000 (death) and ₹12,500 (grievous hurt); the 2019 amendment raised these to ₹2 lakh and ₹50,000 and dropped the term 'Solatium Fund'.

t: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 was notified on 09.08.2019 and its main provisions came into force from:
e: The Amendment Act was notified on 9 August 2019 and implemented from 1 September 2019; the rules on investigation and settlement of claims (the detailed accident report scheme) came into effect from 1 April 2022.

t: 'Golden hour' as defined in Section 2(12A) of the amended MV Act means:
o: The 48 hours within which the First Accident Report must be filed
The one-hour period within which the police must reach the accident spot
The one-hour period following a traumatic injury during which prompt medical care is most likely to prevent death
The first 24 hours after an accident within which the FIR must be lodged
e: Section 2(12A) defines golden hour as the hour after a traumatic injury with the highest likelihood of preventing death by prompt medical care; s.162 provides for cashless treatment during this period.

t: On receiving information of an accident, what is the first statutory step the insurer must take under Section 149(1)?
o: Lodge a complaint with the police under Section 134
Deposit ₹5,00,000 with the Tribunal under Section 164
Designate an officer to settle the claims relating to that accident
File a written statement before the Tribunal within 90 days
e: Section 149(1) requires the insurer, upon receiving information of the accident from the claimant, the accident information report or otherwise, to designate an officer to settle the claims.

t: The rules framed by the Central Government to give effect to the MV Act 1988 are the:
o: Indian Motor Tariff Rules, 2002
Motor Vehicles (Third Party) Rules, 1988
Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
Road Transport Rules, 1990
e: The Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, along with State rules and the Rules of the Road Regulations, constitute the body of law regulating road transport.

t: Causing grievous hurt by an act endangering life or personal safety (old Section 338 IPC) now falls under:
o: Section 106 BNS
Section 125(a) BNS
Section 281 BNS
Section 125(b) BNS
e: Section 337 IPC (hurt) → s.125(a) BNS; Section 338 IPC (grievous hurt) → s.125(b) BNS.

t: 'Community service' as inserted by Section 2(4A) of the amended Act means:
o: Unpaid work which a person is required to perform as punishment for an offence under the Act
Voluntary service by Good Samaritans at accident sites
Paid work by convicts in road construction
Service by insurers in settling claims at Lok Adalats
e: Section 2(4A) defines community service as unpaid work ordered as punishment for an offence under the MV Act, introduced as an alternative penalty.

t: Under the amended Section 159, the police officer must prepare and submit the accident information report to the Claims Tribunal within:
o: Forty-eight hours
Six months
Thirty days
Three months
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 159 requires the police officer, during investigation, to prepare an accident information report in the prescribed form within three months and submit it to the Claims Tribunal and other prescribed agency.

t: An accident occurs in District A; the claimant resides in District B and the owner of the offending vehicle resides in District C. The claim petition under Section 166 may be filed before the Claims Tribunal of:
o: District C only, where the defendant resides
District A, B or C – at the claimant's option
District B only, where the claimant resides
District A only, where the accident occurred
e: Section 166(2) allows filing before the Tribunal having jurisdiction where the accident occurred, where the claimant resides or carries on business, or where the defendant resides.
